text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT  :-(English) 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28-32 HRC. 2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The heat treatment note specifies the hardness (28-32 HRC) but does not state at which manufacturing stage it applies (e.g., before or after final machining). This ambiguity can lead to parts being machined in the hardened state or left soft when they should be hard, affecting both manufacturability and function. The designer should add the process stage to the heat treatment callout.","recommended_correction":"Update N3 to specify when the toughening is to be performed relative to machining and surface treatment (e.g., 'TO BE TOUGHENED TO 28-32 HRC AFTER ROUGH MACHINING, BEFORE FINAL GRINDING')."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D6","page":1,"quote":"⌀20"}],"comment":"The part receives a plating/coating finish (I.Z.B.P.) yet the main pin diameter D6 carries no tolerance allowance for the added coating thickness. If this pin functions as a stop pin that fits into a hole, the unplated dimension plus the plating buildup will result in an unintended tighter fit or interference. The designer should either reduce the nominal size by the expected plating thickness or explicitly note that dimensions apply after plating.","recommended_correction":"Add a plating-thickness allowance to D6 or add a note clarifying whether the dimensioned sizes are before or after the I.Z.B.P. surface treatment."}]}
